title: Agent::in_transaction saves twice when its step already saved
description:
Agent::in_transaction ends its step with an unconditional

    self.save()?;

before COMMIT. A step that saved on its own leaves nothing for that
save to write, so the UPDATE of agent_state puts back the bytes
already there inside the transaction.

Measured while fixing mimid-604m.7, on a poll that takes in one
Message. The writes of the agent_state row, read on a second
connection with an AFTER UPDATE trigger that reports whether the
record changed (crates/mimid-agent-core/tests/state_writes.rs):

    changed=true    Agent::handle_message's own save, inside the
                    transaction: the Message marked handled
    changed=false   in_transaction's save after the step
    changed=true    the poll's last save: the Message state read up to

So one no-op UPDATE per received Message remains. It dirties a page
inside a transaction that is committing anyway, so it costs no extra
commit and no extra fsync, which is why mimid-604m.7 left it: the
pre-save was a transaction of its own and this is not.

The same condition would cover it (the record equals the row and the
journal is empty), but the argument is not the same one: inside the
transaction there is no recovery point to reason about, and the
callers that rely on the post-save to persist what their step changed
have not been looked at. For Mark.
